clue.text: Newspaper containing excellent feature

indicators.note: the newspaper holds the next word inside it, as a paper contains a story

blocks.note: the Financial Times, known by its initials
ace means first-rate

explanation.surface: A paper carries a story that is a particularly fine piece of journalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' looks like a newspaper article, which suits the surface, but here it means an aspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one aspect or side of something, which is what a feature is in the sense of a characteristic.

clue.text: Little female real nasty

blocks.note: f is the short form of female, and little signals the abbreviation
the rightful owner is the real, legitimate one

explanation.surface: Slangy talk of a small woman who is really spiteful: 'real nasty'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Real nasty' reads as one slangy phrase, but 'real' is wordplay and 'nasty' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightful and nasty are synonyms, both meaning very unpleasant or dreadful.

clue.text: One managing to be PC in a half-hearted way

blocks.note: a PC is a police constable, a cop
er is the noise of someone speaking hesitantly

explanation.surface: Someone gets by being only lukewarmly politically correct.
explanation.walkthrough: PC suggests political correctness in the surface; in the wordplay it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A coper is someone who copes, that is, who manages to deal with difficulties.

clue.text: Protection from criminal student going around

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround it, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a tutee is a student taught by a tutor
an old lag is a habitual convict

explanation.surface: Someone seeks safety from a lawbreaking student who is on the prowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' reads as part of the definition's phrase but only joins it to the wordplay. Lag is British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is guardianship, the protective care of a guardian over a ward.

clue.text: Haul around piece of furniture that's easily managed

indicators.note: turning around makes the word face the other way, so it is read from its end

blocks.note: to cart something is to haul it
a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: Furniture that is light enough to drag about the room without trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractable describes something docile or easy to handle and control.

clue.text: Kicked and pulled? Wife will leave!

indicators.note: whatever leaves goes away, so that letter is taken out of the word

blocks.note: towed means pulled along
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A violent marriage, kicked and dragged about, ends with the wife walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the W from TOWED to leave TOED.
explanation.definitionFit: To toe something is to touch or kick it with the toes, so toed is kicked.

clue.text: Worker with a heart keeps on being a hostile opponent

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the heart word holds the next word within it

blocks.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
taken as written
the gist is the heart of a matter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted worker who keeps going despite a hostile opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: ANT and A, then GIST holding ON: G(ON)IST.
explanation.definitionFit: An antagonist is an adversary, someone who actively opposes another.

clue.text: Little kid must stifle word of scorn, as well

indicators.note: stifling something smothers it, so the outer word wraps around the inner one

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
boo is a jeer of derision

explanation.surface: A small child has to suppress a jeer as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase to boot is an idiom for in addition or besides.

clue.text: Geese Alec disturbed in farm buildings

indicators.note: something disturbed has been upset from its settled state, so these letters are rearranged
the jumbled letters are placed inside the buildings word

blocks.note: barns are farm buildings
taken as written, then shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone named Alec scared some geese in the farmyard sheds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Geese' looks like part of the farm scene, but it is the definition: the barnacle goose is a species.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnacles is a name for barnacle geese, a black-and-white Arctic goose species.

clue.text: Leave each time without being first

indicators.note: placing something first means it goes at the start of the answer

blocks.note: ex is Latin for out of, meaning without
ea is the abbreviation for each
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Taking time off every time but never being the first to go.
explanation.walkthrough: An exeat is the formal permission British boarding schools and colleges grant for a pupil to be away.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is a leave of absence, from the Latin for 'let him go out'.

clue.text: I am glaring — one caught being restive

indicators.note: something caught is held fast inside another thing

blocks.note: I am contracts to I'm
patent means obvious, as in a glaring mistake
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone staring angrily admits to being caught while fidgeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glaring' suggests staring angrily, but here it means obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Restive and impatient both describe someone restless and unwilling to wait.

clue.text: Support for ballet voiced by pub

indicators.note: voiced means spoken out loud, so it is the sound of a word that counts

blocks.note: a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub announces it is backing the ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: A barre is the horizontal rail dancers hold for balance during ballet exercises.

clue.text: Only just a brief line famous author's penned

indicators.note: something penned is enclosed, as in a pen, so it sits inside the author's name

blocks.note: Thomas Hardy, the English novelist
l is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A great novelist wrote just the shortest possible line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like writing, but here it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly means barely or scarcely, only just.

clue.text: A grin not somehow blissful?

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unspecified way, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A smile that is not quite happy?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: 'where ignorance is bliss', so the ignorant are blissful.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'ignorance is bliss' means those unaware of trouble are happy, so blissful hints at lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Emphatic form of words ending little folks' letter?

blocks.note: a letter is customarily signed off 'Yours'
elves are the little people of folklore

explanation.surface: Children's letters end with an emphatic flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter from the little folk would close 'Yours, Elves', and the question mark admits the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Yourselves is the emphatic or reflexive form of the plural pronoun you, as in 'see it yourselves'.

clue.text: In favour of canon being without say or position of prominence

indicators.note: being outside means standing next to rather than within, so the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: for means supporting
e.g. means for example, as say does
a canon is a musical round

explanation.surface: Backing the cathedral clergy without a word, or holding a prominent position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' suggests a cleric, but here it is the musical form where voices enter in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The foreground is the part of a scene nearest the viewer, hence the most prominent place.

clue.text: Trickery to get new leader in party

indicators.note: getting a new leader means the first letter is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: deception is trickery

explanation.surface: Underhand dealings bring a new leader into the political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political, but it is a social gathering. The clue leaves the new first letter open; the crossings fix it as R.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is a formal social gathering, a kind of party.

clue.text: Card that may give members benefits

blocks.note: first meaning: a playing card of the black suit with the clover symbol
second meaning: a society whose members enjoy its facilities

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a membership card; the card and the society are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a playing card of one suit and an association that offers privileges to its members.

clue.text: Top jockey gets these and dominates

blocks.note: top means best
a jockey is given mounts to ride

explanation.surface: The leading rider gets the choice mounts and wins everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it says the top jockey gets the best rides.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride something is to straddle or tower over it, hence to dominate.

clue.text: In the clan, a bit cheeky, needing final change of direction

indicators.note: a change of direction swaps right for left, and final says it is the last letter that changes

blocks.note: familiar means overly informal, slightly impertinent

explanation.surface: Within the family, someone is rather cheeky and needs a final change of course.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L are the abbreviations for right and left, so switching direction swaps the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Familial means relating to a family, so belonging to the clan.

clue.text: Chance to show courage, not keeping quiet

indicators.note: not keeping something means letting it go, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: pluck means bravery
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An opportunity for someone to prove their bravery without staying silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Luck is chance, the force that brings good or bad fortune by accident.

clue.text: It's very Parisian, getting amorous advances — may they be forgiven!

blocks.note: très is French for very
to make a pass is to make an amorous approach

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's romantic overtures, which one hopes will be pardoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition echoes the Lord's Prayer: 'forgive us our trespasses'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespasses are sins or wrongs, which the Lord's Prayer asks to be forgiven.

clue.text: Class that's offered short trip

blocks.note: a sort is a class or kind
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A school class gets offered a brief excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a short outing or excursion, originally a military sally.

clue.text: Pop, a Rev., moved to get daughter confirmed

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted out of their places into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
d is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A father who is a vicar has his daughter confirmed in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Confirmation suggests the church rite here; the definition means ratified.
explanation.definitionFit: Something approved has been officially sanctioned or confirmed.

clue.text: A medic going around hospital for a particular case

indicators.note: going around something means encircling it, so the doctor encloses the hospital letter

blocks.note: taken as written
doc is short for doctor
H is the map symbol for hospital

explanation.surface: A doctor does a ward round in hospital to see one particular patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' fits the medical scene as a patient; the definition is a Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc is Latin for 'for this', describing something arranged for one specific purpose.

clue.text: Drink taster can be heard

indicators.note: what can be heard is what is spoken, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: one who licks something gets a taste of it

explanation.surface: A wine taster's job announced out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is alcoholic drink, especially spirits.

clue.text: The woman entertained by old city guide

indicators.note: a guest who is entertained is received inside the host's home

blocks.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword staple
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A female tourist is welcomed by a guide in an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats, so leads or guides them.

clue.text: One to get hammered making money heartlessly

indicators.note: without a heart, the central letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: A ruthless moneymaker who will end up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' suggests drunk; the definition is something struck with a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brad is a thin small-headed wire nail, driven in with a hammer.

clue.text: Person to present show — one stuck in lift

indicators.note: something stuck inside is lodged within, so the letter sits inside the other word

blocks.note: a host presents a TV show
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A TV presenter ends up trapped in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' reads as a British elevator in the surface but is a verb or noun meaning raise.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is a device for lifting heavy things, and to hoist is to raise.

clue.text: After very bad rain outhouse is given protective coating

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong and spoilt, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: v is the abbreviation for very
the letters to be rearranged
a shed is a small outbuilding

explanation.surface: After a downpour, the garden shed gets a new protective coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very bad' looks like one phrase, but 'very' is the letter and 'bad' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnished means coated with a clear resin finish that protects wood.

clue.text: Study in second form, being thicker

indicators.note: a new form of a word is a reshaping, so its letters are rearranged
the study word goes inside the reshaped letters

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: A pupil studying in the second form at school, being rather dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second form' suggests a school year, but 'form' signals rearranging 'second'. 'Thicker' means dense, not stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Condensed means made denser or more concentrated, as condensed milk is thickened.

clue.text: Primate, one taking place of duke in upper house

indicators.note: taking someone's place means replacing them, so one letter swaps for another

blocks.note: the House of Lords is Britain's upper parliamentary chamber
the Roman numeral for one
d is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: An archbishop replaces a duke in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, who might sit in the Lords; here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The loris is a small slow-moving nocturnal primate of South and Southeast Asia.
